--- title: "[StepDropCorr]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Remove numeric columns whose pairwise absolute correlation is too high. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/step_drop_corr.py#L159-L302){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StepDropCorr(columns, threshold=0.9, method="pearson", id=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The selected columns that exceed ``threshold`` are dropped, as are columns with no usable correlation at all (constant or all-null), and no new columns are produced. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Selector]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns to consider for removal. Accepts a single column name, a list of names, a shoez selector such as ``Selectors.numeric_predictors()`` (see `Selectors` for the full set), or a narwhals or polars selector (``narwhals.selectors.numeric()``, ``polars.selectors.numeric()``). Selectors are resolved against the frame's schema when the recipe is fitted, so the same selector works on any backend. Only numeric columns are meaningful here. [threshold]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.9]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Pairs whose absolute correlation is strictly above this value trigger a removal. Default ``0.9``. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Literal[["pearson"]{.st}, ["spearman"]{.st}]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["pearson"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Correlation method: ``"pearson"`` (default) or ``"spearman"``. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stable step identifier. Default ``"corr"``. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ``a`` and ``b`` are almost perfectly correlated, so one of them is dropped; the uncorrelated ``c`` is kept: ::: {#6f55db84 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame( { "a": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], "b": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.1], "c": [4.0, 1.0, 3.0, 2.0], } ) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
a b c
0 1.0 1.0 4.0
1 2.0 2.0 1.0
2 3.0 3.0 3.0
3 4.0 4.1 2.0
``` ::: ::: Specifying the step touches no data: ::: {#4ac54c62 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepDropCorr(s.numeric_predictors(), threshold=0.9)) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: no roles assigned Steps: step_drop_corr(select(role='predictor', type=NumericType)) [untrained] ``` ::: ::: `fit()` computes the correlation matrix and picks the columns to drop: ::: {#23f5c2e5 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Recipe (trained) Inputs: 2 columns — 2 predictors Steps: step_drop_corr(a, b, c) [trained] ``` ::: ::: `transform()` drops them: ::: {#03020e62 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
b c
0 1.0 4.0
1 2.0 1.0
2 3.0 3.0
3 4.1 2.0
``` ::: ::: A ``threshold`` above their correlation keeps both: ::: {#f40ee9db .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepDropCorr(s.numeric_predictors(), threshold=0.9999)) fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
a b c
0 1.0 1.0 4.0
1 2.0 2.0 1.0
2 3.0 3.0 3.0
3 4.0 4.1 2.0
``` ::: :::
